h: First time in an escape room?
p: If you've never done one before, don't panic. You don't need to be a genius, a detective or a puzzle fanatic. The rooms are designed so that a group of normal people, chatting away and checking every nook, can get through with the odd nudge. The biggest mistake first-timers make is everyone crowding round the same puzzle, so spread out, search different corners and shout about anything that looks odd. Numbers, colours and symbols almost always mean something.

It also helps to pick a theme that suits your group. A spooky storyline might be a laugh for a gang of mates but less fun for younger players, so have a look at the room descriptions together before you book and go for one that everyone's excited about.

Festival Place makes the logistics easy, with parking, food and loos all close by. Once you're done, there's more around Basingstoke worth a look. Milestones Museum on the Leisure Park recreates streets from Victorian and later times and is a hit with families, while the Anvil is the town's well-known concert hall if you fancy a show in the evening. For a breather, Eastrop Park is a short walk from the shopping centre, with green space and water to wander beside, and the War Memorial Park offers a bit more room to roam. Top of Town, the older part of Basingstoke around Market Place, is worth a mooch too.
